content: A somatic cell refers to any cell that constitutes the body of an organism. The term somatic originates from the Greek word sōma (σώμα), which translates to body. By definition, somatic cells are distinct from germline cells. In mammals, germline cells include spermatozoa and ova (commonly referred to as gametes), which unite during fertilization to form a zygote. This zygote is the single cell from which the entire mammalian embryo develops. All other cell types in the mammalian body, excluding sperm, ova, the precursor cells that produce them (gametocytes), and undifferentiated stem cells, are classified as somatic cells. Examples of somatic cells include those that make up internal organs, skin, bones, blood, and connective tissues. In terms of genetics and chromosomal composition, somatic cells can be simply defined as non-sex cells, though this is a broad and not entirely precise description. In humans, somatic cells contain a total of 46 chromosomes, organized into 23 pairs. Each pair consists of one chromosome inherited from the father and one from the mother. This means that human somatic cells have twice the number of chromosomes as germline cells, which contain only 23 unpaired chromosomes. During conception, germline cells fuse to form a zygote, which then contains 46 chromosomes (or 23 pairs). The sex of the resulting individual is determined by the specific sex chromosome (X or Y) contributed by the germline cells. Humans, along with other species whose somatic cells have chromosomes arranged in pairs, are classified as diploid organisms. In contrast, their germline cells, which contain only single, unpaired chromosomes, are referred to as haploid. However, in other species, chromosomal arrangements can be more complex. For instance, some species have somatic cells with chromosomes arranged in sets of four (tetraploid) or even six (hexaploid). This means their germline cells can be diploid or even triploid. A notable example is the modern cultivated wheat species, Triticum aestivum L., which is a hexaploid organism. Its somatic cells contain six copies of each chromosome.
